source.title: Multimodal Representation Alignment for Cross-modal Information Retrieval

record.tranche_reason: The study measures image–text representation alignment and tests how geometric measures, retrieval metrics, and datasets relate to it. It does not reproduce a scale sweep.
record.gate_note: The study compares paired image and text representations, but does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or independently measured model capability. It compares Euclidean modality gaps, Wasserstein-2 distances, cosine-similarity matrices, and retrieval outcomes. Table 3 and Table 4 contain many flattened retrieval values; only the authors' explicit qualitative metric comparison is recorded here rather than assigning ambiguous cells to models.
record.test_reason: The study's own geometric and paired-similarity results bear on V6: distributional proximity and high absolute cosine similarity can fail to indicate semantic alignment. It does not test increasing convergence with capability, and alignment deliberately learned through paired contrastive training is not evidence of spontaneous convergence.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that smaller modality gaps do not necessarily predict retrieval quality, cosine works best for the tested contrastively trained VLMs, and their custom contrastive objective generally improves learned scoring over MSE. They acknowledge architecture- and dataset-dependent exceptions. These are retrieval and alignment-method conclusions, not evidence that independent models converge more with scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares cross-modal geometry and retrieval across pretrained VLMs and paired unimodal encoders, and trains scoring networks with MSE or a custom contrastive loss. It does not apply the original sources' convergence measurement or test a scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, retrieval direction, encoder, and similarity metric. Transformer results also vary with attention-head count and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Cosine generally yields the best CLIP/BLIP retrieval, while retrieval varies with encoder, dataset, and direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal retrieval performance depends on the scoring metric and evaluation setting.

fits_no_version.finding: CLIP and BLIP show paired diagonals, whereas separately trained unimodal encoders and Meta-Transformer do not in these coordinates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Paired contrastive pretraining is associated with directly discriminative image-text similarities in the tested output spaces.

fits_no_version.finding: Custom contrastive training improves learned pair scoring over MSE overall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised pair-scoring networks benefit from a discriminative objective rather than imitation of cosine scores.

record.problems: No model-scale or independent capability analysis. The cosine-similarity matrices use 10 randomly selected pairs for visualization. Exact results in Tables 3 and 4 are difficult to assign from the flattened text rendering; the paper does report statistical comparisons, but this record does not infer ambiguous table cells.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 3 and 4 contain many separate retrieval scores for model, metric, dataset, direction, and Recall@K; these were not transcribed because the supplied flattened layout does not reliably assign every number to its model and metric. Tables 5 and 6 and the appendix retrieval examples were also omitted as they do not add direct measures of representation convergence beyond the recorded metric and alignment findings.

untested.parts: No scale or independently measured capability sweep; no test of increasing alignment among independently trained models.
No test that paired image-caption alignment increases as both encoders improve. CLIP and BLIP were deliberately trained for cross-modal alignment; static alignment is insufficient.
No comparison across initializations of the same architecture.
No representation substitution, stitching, or simple mapping with measured preservation of another model's function. The learned networks output pair scores.
No comparison of interpretable features or circuits.

No controlled out-of-distribution test, neighbour-count sweep, or test that a scale-dependent convergence trend disappears under another metric. Evidence concerns adequacy of cross-modal alignment measurements.

No convergence plateau, calibrated completeness estimate, or controlled separation of training-data and objective effects. The contrastive-training explanation is plausible interpretation, not a causal test; nonzero modality gaps do not establish incomplete shared subspaces.

missing.what: Add an explicit comparative result recording that distributional and centroid distances do not fully characterize paired semantic alignment. Individual distance rows currently leave this essential V6 result implicit.
missing.locator: Section 4.3, final paragraph; Section 4.4; Figures 2–3 and Table 2

record.verdict_notes: All numerical geometry rows match the supplied text. Agreement between Euclidean and Wasserstein broad trends does not warrant limits_scope for V6, which does not require every metric to disagree. Dataset variation in retrieval does not establish out-of-distribution weakening of convergence. Learned scorers consume both representations and output one scalar; they do not demonstrate interchangeable representations.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep; no comparison of alignment across increasing scale.
Tests paired image–text representations across selected encoders and datasets, but not whether alignment rises as both encoders improve or scale.
No independently initialized seeds or shared-feature/subspace analysis.
The learned networks score image–text pairs; they do not map one model's representations into another's.
No interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are compared.
Tests metric and dataset variation in the studied image–text retrieval setting; does not test out-of-distribution inputs or neighbour-count settings.
Findings bear on incomplete alignment and the role of contrastive training, but do not experimentally separate shared data, shared objectives, and a common model of reality as causes.

rows.subject: CLIP
rows.operation_detail: Compared standard and learned similarity metrics for image–text retrieval

conditions.value: Reported across datasets and retrieval directions

rows.measure: Retrieval performance under alternative similarity metrics
rows.value: Cosine similarity works best for CLIP; the authors report that cosine consistently outperforms the investigated alternatives for VLM representations.
rows.uncertainty: Pairwise comparisons: p < .001 for CLIP/BLIP cosine versus other models; no uncertainty stated for this qualitative metric summary.
rows.note: The underlying Tables 3 and 4 report disaggregated results; exact cells are not assigned here because the supplied table layout is flattened.
rows.check: This measures retrieval performance under alternative scoring methods, not convergence between models. Comparisons with learned scorers also change training and candidate-set sizes. The reported p < .001 concerns CLIP/BLIP versus other encoder models, not every within-CLIP metric comparison.

relationships.condition: Meta-Transformer across IMDB, Flickr30K, and MS-COCO: absolute cosine similarity versus matched-pair discrimination
relationships.reason: R39, R45, and R51 report cosine above 0.9 for every pair without a discriminative diagonal, showing that high absolute similarity can misleadingly suggest alignment.
relationships.display_finding: Cosine similarity exceeded 0.9 for every pair without distinguishing matched pairs from mismatches.

relationships.condition: Distribution-level proximity versus paired semantic alignment in the tested encoders
relationships.reason: R03, R09, R15, R21, R27, and R33 show relatively close Meta-Transformer distributions, while R39, R45, and R51 lack paired discrimination; Section 4.3 explicitly concludes that these distances cannot fully characterize alignment.
relationships.display_finding: Meta-Transformer distributions were relatively close despite lacking matched-pair discrimination, so distribution distances did not fully characterize semantic alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CLIP and BLIP on IMDB, Flickr30K, and MS-COCO
reader_labels.reason: Both contrastively trained VLMs show clear diagonals for paired image–text similarities in the reported matrices (R37, R38, R43, R44, R49, R50).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Meta-Transformer and combined unimodal encoders across the three datasets
reader_labels.reason: The sampled similarity matrices lack a discriminative paired diagonal for these encoders; Meta-Transformer instead gives uniformly high scores (R39-R42, R45-R48, R51-R54).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Retrieval metric choice for CLIP and BLIP
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that cosine performs best among the investigated retrieval metrics for these VLMs (R55-R56).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Euclidean modality gap compared with Wasserstein-2 distance
reader_labels.reason: The reported broad trend is similar for these two geometric measures, so this study does not show that every reasonable measure changes the conclusion (R01-R36; authors' comparison in Section 4.3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Contrastively trained VLMs versus Meta-Transformer and combined unimodal encoders
reader_labels.reason: The VLMs show paired-image/text diagonal structure, whereas other representations do not; the authors attribute the former pattern to contrastive training and warn that Meta-Transformer's high similarities are not discriminative (R37-R54).
